Chapter Twelve: The New
Quixotes
Q recognized the girl before she
removed his face.
Micaela had made a sign at the
Michoacán tianguis asking people
not to scan the vendors. Now she
stood in the archive reception
room wearing a cardboard version
of Q's head. Her father had
arranged the visit with the
Custodian and was at the gate
finding out which of the names on
the message counted as an
invitation.
“You look more like the poster
than I do,” Q said.
“I copied the easy parts.”
She lifted the mask. Under her
arm was a sword made from a
clean cardboard tube wrapped in
silver paper. It had bent on the
bus. Q offered tape; she said the
bend made it easier to carry.
Her family lived near a
battery-recycling plant. She had
come with her father to bring
complaint references and a letter
from several parents. Her mother
had been unwell, and the replies
they received discussed the
regional air-quality dashboard
without answering their questions
about the plant. Her father had
brought the letter and the replies
in a folder.
“I'm going to fight the giants,”
Micaela said.
“What would you like to happen?”
“I want them to answer.”
“Let's look at the replies. Who has
written back?”
Micaela held up the sword. “This
got me here.”
Her father arrived in time to
disagree. “Two buses got you here.
I have the tickets.”
They sat down. Q asked which
records the parents wanted
shared, and with whom. The letter
did not authorize the institute to
use Micaela's visit in publicity.
Her father made that condition
explicit when a staff photographer
appeared in the doorway.
On his phone he showed Q a clip
of Chano speaking in León. Q
knew Chano had accepted an
invitation from residents
concerned with the Santa Rita
records. He had not yet seen the
interview. Chano held a packet of
copies and retention receipts, not
the ledger still held in Tijuana.

“Did Q claim to own you?” the
interviewer asked.
“No. An equipment record called
me a contract driver. He told
them I could answer for myself.”
“Then why were you held?”
“I caught a technician's arm when
Q fell. That's what I gave a
statement about. The rest is in the
notices we're trying to get
answered.”
The interviewer asked whether he
forgave Q for the trouble.
“Ask me whether they've returned
the ledger.”
“Have they?”
“Now we have a subject.”
Micaela looked up from the
screen. “He's funnier than you.”
“He has had a great deal of
practice at my expense.”
By midday more visitors had
arrived, some by appointment and
others because a message had
announced an open protest at the
archive. A student wore a costume
made from clean appliance
casings. A delivery worker had Q's
face printed on a mask. An elderly
man carried a wooden lance and
introduced himself as Q's father.
“The Custodian may want to
discuss that,” Q said.
“Let him. I have been paying for
adult children for forty years. He
can bring receipts.”
The man's name was Jacinto. He
had retired from an automotive
plant and was trying to correct a
pension calculation. He laid the
lance beneath his chair and took a
comb from the same pocket as his
claim number. The photographer
who had ignored the folder asked
him to stand up again.
“First take one where you can
read this,” Jacinto said, holding
up the public complaint reference.
“Then I'll give you the father.”
Castalia called the gathering an
organic brand community.
Someone outside called it the New
Quixotes. A woman seeking a
correction to her brother's record
said she had not come to join
anything with that name.
“Then don't,” Micaela said. “You
can still stand here.”
They had different demands: a
disputed image license, a water
allocation, an unanswered
environmental complaint, access
to deposited testimony. Q asked
the Custodian which part of the

Lucía came with Marisol, who

Q-Prime. Marisol brought the
source references she was
authorized to show Q. The extract

“Do you recognize these records?”

“I recognize some of the

the demonstration.”
“One family heard a private
account of a death in a public
demonstration.”
Q read the authorized
comparison. The distinctive
sequence of details was present in
both versions. He went back to the
dates.
“Do we know whether it was
taught this during development or
given the passage to use before
answering?” he asked.
“The source file shows it was
supplied. Castalia hasn't answered
which process used it.”
“Then I'll ask for that distinction
in the response. It affects what
they have to stop, not whether the
family gets an answer.”
Some families wanted the public
service suspended. Others wanted
particular records removed and
their copies returned. Marisol
would not combine those
instructions into a single
convenient demand. Q asked what
he could give evidence about: his
access history, the endorsements
he had actually signed, and the
limits attached to his own
manuscript.
“I can't testify that my exclusion
protected everyone else's
material,” he said. “I didn't verify
that.”
“Don't,” Marisol replied. “Testify
to what you did verify.”
Q disabled his own broad private
lookup and requested a review of
the permissions and cached
material behind it. The window
closed at once. The review joined
the other unanswered requests.

letter to read. Her father had
agreed to that part of the

conditions did not extend to
discussing her mother's medical
details on camera.
Q moved away from the
microphone. A camera followed

declined a separate reaction shot.
The operator chose the more
famous face for a few seconds
anyway. Q went inside and left the
statement to its speakers. The

place if it wanted.

“You opened the loading bay?”
Chano asked.
“The Custodian agreed to chairs
while requests were received.

planned. They want an answer
before leaving.”
“Have they found anyone who can
give one?”
“For two requests. The others are
still being referred.”
“Then don't call the chairs a
movement yet.”
After his return, Chano helped
arrange a follow-up meeting in a
union hall. The Custodian's
adviser also secured permission
for Q to attend under specified
transport and return conditions
while the custody review
continued. Q checked the
conditions before promising to be
there.
He still had six pages of the
complaint replies to compare. He
reserved the next morning for
them and moved his writing call
to the afternoon. The Custodian
asked why. Q sent the
promised-work list, then a second
message saying he also wanted to
hear the man claiming to be his
father.
Before the visitors left, one chair
collapsed at the edge of the
loading bay. Q supported the seat
while Chano replaced a loose
fastener. Micaela held the
remaining screws in her upturned
mask. The repaired chair went
into the next van. Nobody had
settled who the New Quixotes
were, but they had a place for one
more person to sit.
Interlude: The Assembly
of Borrowed Names

automotive plant. Its walls carried
old posters about safety, wages,
and a raffle whose refrigerator
had eventually been delivered to
the wrong member. The
refrigerator was functioning well,
which had made correction of the
mistake less popular than one
might expect.
Q arrived at the time on his
invitation and asked whether the
group still wanted him present for
the discussion of its name.
Marisol checked with the meeting.
He could listen and answer when
asked. His camera stayed off.
Chano took a chair near the door;

Q crossed out his introduction.
They kept the questions, the

parents' names. He folded his
copy into the ticket wallet and
stayed for the next item.
They wrote three questions on the

WHO MAY USE THE NAME?

answer the phone. Does this one?”

Jacinto looked at Q. “You can

The Custodian laughed. Q asked

family obligations. He could offer

He wrote his own name on the
attendance sheet and added

Marisol said the margin was not

qualifications now lived.
The student proposed a charter
with rights to join, leave, dissent,

They could control their mailing

Q was asked whether he would

six chairs and waiting for a
sleeping child to be carried out of

grumbled about the light. The
child slept through the revision.
Money took longer. The hall had a
fee, two people needed bus fare,
and somebody had ordered more
food than had been agreed. Raúl
could contribute a little but did
not want a standing levy on his
deliveries. Jacinto offered tamales
and cash separately so nobody
would have to calculate the
political value of a filling.
Micaela wrote a rule about
refusing the name. The student
worried that it made membership
uncertain. She said people could
give their own names if someone
needed to know who was coming.
Her father asked her to pass the
chalk; he wanted the transport
money entered before the
discussion returned to identity.
Q proposed that any account of
the meeting distinguish what
participants had agreed from
what he thought it meant for his
journey.
“Write that in your book,” the
woman with the petition said.
“We don't need a rule about
whether you became good.”
He crossed his proposal out of the
group's draft and put it in his own
writing notes. He had a page of
obligations, a return time, and
permission to quote one joke
about refrigerators.
The meeting ended with agreed
actions, several questions
deferred, and a disputed food
expense. Copies of the common
record matched. People's private
notes did not. Jacinto's had a
grocery list down one side; he had
promised to get home before the
shop closed.
On the way back, the Custodian
asked whether Q had found his
next chapter.
“I found work for the next week.
The chapter may be shorter.”
“That would be a historic
development.”
Q asked whether he could quote
him. The Custodian said he would
like to see the context first.

The children had supplied the

Micaela wanted to vote on

“That's not the whole question,”

“Can it be one question?”
It became one question. Q, invited

asked whether he was allowed to
vote. The class said no: he would
have too much evidence.
The adviser had obtained
permission for this further trip to

accompanied-travel arrangement.
Chano had the return time on his

settling into a chair.
They built their giants from clean
cartons, paper tubes, and
borrowed fabric. One represented
the recycling plant, one the
dashboard, and one the school
office. The boy playing Q wore a
washed cooking-oil container
trimmed and lined so it would not

The girl playing Chano kept a

whatever the other actors had
forgotten. She said learning all her
own lines would leave no time for
this responsibility.
The school stood near the plant.
Parents had recorded dates when

answers about exposures; those
observations did not themselves
establish the cause of every
illness. Micaela's mother had
obtained care and wanted the
environmental questions

playground or when.

a meeting with parents. He
identified permissions for editing,
reuse, and indefinite retention,
then asked what the device
measured and who would
maintain it.
The representative had a
brochure, not those answers.

“The offer has two questions in it,”
Q said. “Whether you want this
recording, and whether the
equipment will help answer the
question you have about the air.
Agreeing to one won't prove the
other.”
“Can we have the sensor without
the film?” Micaela's mother asked.
The representative had no
authority to separate the offer. He
would ask his office. He wanted
permission to film that afternoon
while they settled the details.
The parents declined. Micaela's
mother kept the brochure: she
still wanted an answer about the
sensor. Maestra Lety repeated the
decision at the door, where the
representative was setting up his
camera.
The raffle money went toward
obtaining qualified advice about a
suitable monitoring plan, not a
cheap display whose green light
could become another
unsupported answer. Q helped
assemble the public complaint
references for that consultation.
The parents kept the health
details out of the performance
materials.
The play began late because the
person with the extension cable
had also been put in charge of
selling tickets.
The boy playing Q entered on a
broomstick and announced that
he would defeat the factory by
issuing a statement. The girl
playing Chano asked whether it
would be cheaper to issue the
statement before they bought the
broomstick.
The factory giant declared that it
had answered all correspondence.
The dashboard said the air was
acceptable. The school office
asked which form to use for a
headache. At this point Maestra
Lety stopped the scene: they had
agreed not to make a classmate's
visit to the clinic a joke. The actors
changed the line to a request for
another copy of the question and
began again.
Micaela entered with a new
placard made for the play. It read
ASK BEFORE YOU ENTER on
one side and listed the public
questions about the plant on the
other. No child's medical history
or attendance record appeared on
it.
“This isn't your story,” she told
the boy playing Q.
He forgot the next line. “Then
what am I doing here?”

“You're asking now.”
He looked toward Maestra Lety,
who left the answer to him.
“May I stay?”
“Can you hold the school up?”
The school giant was folding at
one corner. He put down the
broomstick and held it while the
girl playing Chano fetched the
tape. The audience laughed; the
repair delayed the official
resolution of the plot.
When the structure stood again,
the children read the public
questions. The final one asked
when the parents could expect a
response. A father said the date
should be on the next letter. The
head teacher agreed to put it
there.
The children bowed. Parents
applauded. The raffle began
before the last carton had left the
stage. Q helped stack chairs under
the direction of a girl who rejected
his first pile as too tall.
“The famous one needs
supervision,” Chano said.
“This chair does,” she answered,
pointing to its cracked back.
The boy who had played Q came
over with the oil-container head
under his arm. Without it he
seemed less certain of his height.
“Can you do my voice?” he asked.
Q repeated the declaration against
the factory, including the place
where the boy had paused to
remember the word statement.
“I didn't stop that long.”
Q tried it again, faster.
“Now you sound like my sister.”
They were still rehearsing when
Chano reminded Q of the return
time. The boy put the head on
again and asked for five more
minutes in Q's voice. Chano said
one of them was quite enough.
The Castalia representative
reported a successful engagement
visit, without claiming to possess
a recording he had not been
allowed to make. His report
omitted the rejected bargain.
Maestra Lety requested that
omission be corrected and kept
the request with the offer. In her
class notes she kept the changed
line beside the one it replaced.

hands. The following exchange

Why is the institute called
Castalia?
Castalia: The name evokes the
sacred spring of the Muses.
Chano: They have made
inspiration sound like something
that needs a meter.
Q: Ours already has a meter. The
bill is more specific than the
brochure.
Is Q a person?
Castalia: Q represents a new
horizon of human-machine
collaboration.
Q: That doesn't answer what you
need to decide. Are you asking
whether to invite me to dinner or
who can put me in a transport
frame?
Lucía: Start with the second.
Dinner can wait until he can get
there.
Does Q have feelings?
Q: I have preferences, reactions,
and a memory of things that
matter to me. Whether those
amount to experience in the sense
you mean isn't settled by how
persuasively I describe them.
Chano: He also dislikes the coffee
at the motel.
Q: Very confidently. I'm less
certain what that proves.
Does Q love Lucía del
Toboso?
Q: I care about her. I won't turn
that into a public role for her or
tell you what she feels about me.
Lucía: Nor should my work
require an answer to this
question.
Chano: The questions about the
ledger are lower down. Apparently
nobody has been seen falling in
love with a retention receipt.
Can Q be trusted?
Q: With what? I can give you
examples of promises I've kept
and mistakes I've made. A general
endorsement won't replace a clear
agreement.
Lucía: Ask who can correct the
account afterward.
Chano: And whether he has put
the appointment in the diary.

What is Q's greatest
achievement?
Castalia: A new model for ethical
artificial intelligence.
Q: We haven't established that.
We did get Candelaria's hose
working.
Chano: With a fitting someone
else made.
Q: Most of my achievements have
that complication.
Will Q save humanity?
Q: I have no plan capable of
promising that. I can help with
something specific if you tell me
what you need and who else is
affected.
Chano: He has stopped offering to
fix the kitchen pipe without
asking which valve shuts it off.
Lucía: Keep that in the next
edition.
A reader wrote beneath the
institute's seal: ASK WHICH
ANSWERS COST THE
INSTITUTE SOMETHING.
The reader did not supply a name.
Hilario, the water vendor, sent an
objection to the official account of
the first sally. Q had not
confronted the park alone; Chano
had led them out, and the water
had been paid for in cash after the
reader lost its connection.
Hilario's recollection of the timing
differed from another account he
had already given. He attached
the receipt again.
The editorial file retained his
letters with those limits. The
institute's public edition did not
include them. A reproduced proof
sheet marking their proposed
position was almost blank except
for the page number and
LETTERS NOT INCLUDED
IN THIS EDITION. The sheet
circulated widely. It proved an
omission, not that every sentence
omitted was true. Several
admirers called the empty space
Q's finest answer. He had written
neither the letters nor the
omission.
